name: English A
description: CXC CSEC English A - Reading, Language, Writing, Communication, and Research

topics.title: Comprehension
mustKnow: Read carefully to understand the text
Identify what the passage is about
Answer questions based on the text

examples.question: Read a short passage and answer questions about it
examples.answer: Answers must come from the text
examples.explanation: Always look back at the passage to find answers

commonMistakes: Answering from memory instead of the text

questions.question: What should you do first when answering comprehension questions?
questions.explanation: You must understand the passage before answering

topics.title: Main Ideas
mustKnow: Main idea is what the passage is about
Usually found in the first or last sentence
Supporting details explain the main idea

keyTerms.definition: The central point of a passage
Sentence that states the main idea
Information that explains the main idea

examples.question: A passage about the benefits of exercise. What is the main idea?
examples.answer: Exercise is good for your health
examples.explanation: All details support this central point

commonMistakes: Choosing a detail instead of the main idea
Making the main idea too broad or too narrow
examTips: Ask: What is this passage mainly about?
Look at the first and last sentences

questions.question: The main idea of a passage is:
options: What the passage is mainly about
questions.correctAnswer: What the passage is mainly about
questions.explanation: Main idea is the central message

topics.title: Supporting Details
topics.summary: Finding information that supports the main idea
mustKnow: Details explain or prove the main idea
Look for facts, examples, and reasons
Distinguish between major and minor details

keyTerms.definition: Information that explains the main idea
Facts or examples that support a point
Specific instance that illustrates a point

examples.question: Main idea: Smoking is harmful. What are supporting details?
examples.explanation: These details support why smoking is harmful

examTips: Identify facts that support the main point

questions.question: Supporting details are used to:
questions.explanation: Details support and explain the main point

topics.title: Inference
mustKnow: Inference is understanding what's not directly stated
Combine text clues with your knowledge

examples.question: The sky was dark and people carried umbrellas. What can you infer?
examples.explanation: Dark sky and umbrellas suggest rain

examTips: Look for clues in the text
Use evidence to support your inference

questions.question: She shivered and pulled her coat tighter. What can you infer?
questions.explanation: Shivering and pulling coat tighter suggests cold

topics.title: Context
mustKnow: Use surrounding words to understand meaning

keyTerms.definition: Hint in text about word meaning

examples.question: The arduous climb was difficult and exhausting. What does arduous mean?

questions.question: The benevolent woman gave money to charity. Benevolent means:

topics.title: Author's Purpose
topics.summary: Understanding why the author wrote the text
mustKnow: Authors write to inform, persuade, or entertain
Identify the purpose from the text
Look at the type of writing

examples.question: A news article about climate change. What is the purpose?

examTips: Ask: Why did the author write this?
Look at the type of text

questions.question: An advertisement trying to sell a product has what purpose?
questions.explanation: Advertisements try to convince you to buy

topics.title: Audience
topics.summary: Understanding who the text is for
mustKnow: Audience is who the text is written for

keyTerms.definition: People the text is intended for
Specific group the text aims at

examples.question: A children's book uses simple words. Who is the audience?

questions.question: A medical journal uses technical terms. The audience is:

examples.question: The author uses words like 'terrible' and 'disaster'. What is the tone?

questions.question: Words like 'wonderful' and 'amazing' suggest what tone?

topics.title: Mood
topics.summary: Understanding the feeling created in the reader
mustKnow: Mood is the feeling the text creates

examples.question: Dark, stormy night in a story creates what mood?

examTips: How does the text make you feel?

questions.question: Sunny day, birds singing, children laughing. What mood?

topics.title: Argument
mustKnow: Argument presents a claim with support

examples.question: School should start later because students need more sleep. What is the claim?
examples.explanation: This is the main point being argued

topics.title: Grammar
mustKnow: Grammar is the rules of language

keyTerms.definition: Who or what the sentence is about

examples.question: Correct: 'She goes to school' or 'She go to school'?

topics.title: Sentence Structure
mustKnow: Complex sentences have main and dependent clauses

keyTerms.definition: Complete thought with subject and verb
Group of words with subject and verb
Group of words without subject and verb

examples.question: Identify the subject and verb: 'The dog barks loudly'
examples.explanation: Dog is who, barks is the action

topics.title: Parts of Speech

keyTerms.definition: Names a person, place, or thing

examples.question: Identify parts of speech: 'The quick brown fox jumps'

examTips: Ask what function the word serves

topics.title: Agreement

examples.question: Correct: 'The boy runs' or 'The boy run'?

examTips: Check if subject is singular or plural

examples.question: Change to past: 'I walk to school'
Find synonym for 'happy'
Add punctuation: 'where are you going'
Write argument: Should homework be banned?
examples.answer: Take position, give reasons, address opposition

questions.question: What should an argumentative essay include?
questions.explanation: Arguments need clear position and support

examples.question: Persuade readers to recycle
examples.answer: Use facts, emotional appeals, call to action

examples.question: Explain how photosynthesis works
Write about a memorable day

questions.question: Essential elements of narrative writing include:

topics.title: Descriptive Writing
mustKnow: Include sight, sound, smell, taste, touch

examples.question: Describe a beach at sunset
Write about Caribbean history

topics.title: Audience and Purpose
topics.summary: Understanding who and why we communicate

examples.question: Explaining to a child vs explaining to a doctor
Job interview vs talking to friends
examples.answer: Formal register for interview, informal for friends

examples.question: Change to formal: 'Hey, what's up?'
examples.explanation: Formal language is polite and complete

topics.title: Informal Language

examples.question: Change to informal: 'I am going to the store'

commonMistakes: Using informal language in formal contexts

examples.question: Which is more reliable: academic journal or random blog?
Summarize a long article in 50 words

topics.title: Paraphrasing

examples.question: Paraphrase: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog'
examples.answer: A fast brown fox leaps across a sleepy dog

commonMistakes: Changing only one or two words

questions.question: Paraphrasing means:
questions.explanation: Paraphrase keeps meaning but changes words

keyTerms.definition: Prejudice in favor of one side

examples.question: Website from 1999 about computers. Is it reliable?
